finding: Five latent genomic factors across 14 disorders: Compulsive, schizophrenia-bipolar, neurodevelopmental, internalizing, substance-use; about 66% of genetic variance explained on average
Systematic review of 164 neuroimaging studies found replicated correlates for p-factor, externalizing, thought disorder, internalizing, distress and depression dimensions
Real-world outpatient DSM cross-cutting symptom data showed shared general psychopathology plus mood/anxiety/depression/psychosis/substance/distress-disconnection dimensions
General psychopathology factor is reproducible across modelling approaches but its biological/clinical meaning requires criterion validation
Disinhibited and antagonistic externalizing spectra have substantial validity/utility literature and cut across substance and personality diagnoses
ADHD symptom components map differently to externalizing, neurodevelopmental and internalizing spectra, arguing against a unitary placement
HiTOP psychosis superspectrum structure has been critiqued; thought disorder/detachment arrangement is not settled
Autoimmune psychosis criteria and neuropsychiatric checklist support identifiable immune etiologies in selected psychiatric presentations
Recursive MDD/TRD review supports multiaxial structure and MDD-wide endotypes but not one TRD disease
Recursive schizophrenia review supports etiologic exceptions, transdiagnostic psychosis endotypes, dimensions and TRS treatment state
